A key argument for prioritizing human welfare over corporate profit in globalized economies is that untrammeled globalization has demonstrably exacerbated inequality within many countries. While trade and capital flows have lifted some people out of poverty, particularly in Asia, they have also led to job losses, stagnant wages, and widening income gaps in advanced economies.
